### rdomains: Get the category of content hosted by a domain


#### Install and Load the package

The latest development version of the package will always be on GitHub. To install the package from GitHub and to load the installed package:

```{r, eval=FALSE, install}
remotes::install_github("themains/rdomains")
```

To install the package from CRAN, type in:

```{r, eval=FALSE, cran_install}
install.packages("rdomains")
```

Next, load the package:

```{r, eval=FALSE, load_pkg}
library(rdomains)
```

#### Classify fetched content

Install `reticulate` and Python `piedomains>=0.15.0` in a Python 3.12+ environment.
The bridge passes raw HTML to the Python text classifier and reports its checkpoint
revision. It preserves fetch outcomes separately from classification outcomes.

```{r, eval=FALSE, content}
reticulate::py_install("piedomains>=0.15.0", pip = TRUE)
pages <- collect_content(c("cnn.com", "wikipedia.org"))
classified <- pie_cat(pages = pages)
fetch_report(classified)
classified[c("domain_name", "pie_category", "status", "model_repo", "model_revision")]
```

The checkpoint has known retail/drugs confusion; see its
[model card](https://huggingface.co/gojiberries/piedomains-text).
Thresholded alternatives are not independently validated labels.

#### Source dates

```{r, vintage}
library(rdomains)
source_vintage()
```

Publication dates and download times are separate. Download helpers write metadata
sidecars bound to the data file's checksum. Caller files without matching metadata
have unknown dates. The archived DMOZ snapshot dates to 2015 and Shallalist to January
2022. A domain can change owners after a label was assigned.

#### Shalla

To get category of the content from Shallalist (service discontinued - using archived data), first download the archived data using:

```{r, eval=FALSE, down_shalla}
get_shalla_data()
```

And then, get the category using:

```{r, eval=FALSE, shalla}
shalla_cat("http://www.google.com")
```


#### DMOZ

To get category of the content from DMOZ, first download the archived parsed CSV file using:

```{r, eval=FALSE, down_dmoz}
get_dmoz_data()
```

And then, get the category using:

```{r, eval=FALSE, dmoz}
dmoz_cat("http://www.google.com")
```

#### ML

The bundled adult model uses the domain name and suffix alone. Its artifact dates
to 2017; its probabilities have not been calibrated on current domains:

```{r, eval=FALSE, ml}
adult_ml1_cat("http://www.google.com")
```


#### VirusTotal

Start by getting the API key from [VirusTotal](https://www.virustotal.com/).

The package uses the VirusTotal API v3 for comprehensive domain analysis:

```{r, eval=FALSE, virustotal}
virustotal_cat("http://www.google.com")
```

#### OpenAI GPT Models

OpenAI infers categories from domain names without fetching the page. You need an
OpenAI API key. Failed, truncated or invalid answers return `NA` with a warning:

```{r, eval=FALSE, openai}
# Set your API key
Sys.setenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "your-api-key-here")

# Classify domains
openai_cat("google.com")
```


You can also specify custom categories:

```{r, eval=FALSE, openai_custom}
openai_cat(c("amazon.com", "github.com"),
  categories = c("ecommerce", "technology", "social", "other")
)
```

#### Anthropic Claude

Claude also infers categories from domain names without fetching the page. You need
an Anthropic API key:

```{r, eval=FALSE, claude}
# Set your API key
Sys.setenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "your-api-key-here")

# Classify domains
claude_cat("facebook.com")
```
